1: [The Mul Mantar — The root formula of Sikh faith]
There is but One God, the Eternal, the Creator; Self-existent, without fear, without enmity.
Timeless, unborn, self-existent; Great and bountiful is He.
Known by the grace of the Guru; true in the beginning, true through the ages, He alone is true, and ever shall be true.
2: [Japji, opening stanzas — By thinking, He cannot be known]
By thinking, He cannot be reduced to thought, even by thinking hundreds of thousands of times.
By remaining silent, inner silence is not obtained, even by remaining lovingly absorbed deep within.
The hunger of the hungry is not appeased, even by piling up loads of worldly goods.
So how shall we know the Truth? How shall we rend the veil of falsehood?
O Nanak, thus it is written: walk in the way of His will.
3: Hundreds of thousands of clever tricks, but not even one of them will go along with you in the end.
So how can you become truthful? And how can the veil of illusion be torn away?
O Nanak, it is written that you shall obey the Hukam, His order, His will, and walk in the way of His command.
